text:
marie (design): quick ping — heatmap rows in Errors overview feel visually flat. users skim the list and miss the entry action. thinking of introducing a left-aligned primary affordance so the row reads: CTA | meta | timestamp. thoughts?

aaron (product): saw this on the demo. +1 — the current "three-dots" is too subtle. left affordance might improve scan. maybe use a small label not just icon.

sam (eng-runtime): fine from infra side but note we use a virtualized list. keep per-row DOM minimal (one interactive node ideally).

marie (design): initial proposal: icon + short label "View details" left, keep count + brief message center, time right. increase hit area to meet touch target. quick CSS mock:```css
.heatmap-row{display:flex;align-items:center;padding:8px 12px}
.heatmap-cta{width:36px;height:36px;border-radius:6px;margin-right:10px}
```

olivia (a11y): accessibility checklist: 1) CTA contrast >= 4.5:1 on default background; 2) interactive target >=44x44px; 3) aria-label should include error type + count; 4) provide visible focus outline (recommend 3px thick). Also avoid making the icon-only button ambiguous for screen readers.

aaron (product): tiny copy nit — prefer "View details" over "Open". clearer when people jump to metrics.

marie (design): +1 on copy. also propose visual hierarchy: slightly darker row title, lighter metadata, subtle divider. colors suggestion: icon #0B5FFF, title #111827, meta #6B7280.

sam (eng-runtime): implementation notes: we can do a single tabbable CTA per row using roving tabindex; arrow keys can navigate rows. virtualization will require storing current focus index outside row components. Also prefer aria-hidden on decorative SVGs and an offscreen <span> for SR reading.

olivia (a11y): roving tabindex is good. ensure keyboard users can arrow through without hitting other controls. Also ensure screenreader users hear: "View details for TypeError — 34 occurrences — opens new pane".

marie (design): question: should CTA be left or keep it right but larger? left feels more scan-friendly but breaks existing visual rhythm. open to quick A/B.

aaron (product): propose A/B on staging: left-CTA vs right-expanded CTA for 2 weeks. measure click-through to drilldowns and time-to-first-detail. if left wins, ship small layout change.

sam (eng-runtime): timeline — I can prototype keyboard nav + left-CTA compatibility in next sprint cycle (2 weeks). will validate virtualization perf.

marie (design): I'll upload comps for both variants and an a11y checklist. will include hover/focus states and microcopy strings. attaching design doc: https://go/redwood/design/error-heatmap-entry-affordance

dev-bot: design spec created: https://go/redwood/design/error-heatmap-entry-affordance (notify: #design)

aaron (product): decision summary: run 2-week A/B on staging with metrics (CTR, keyboard nav use, screenreader feedback). If successful, proceed with rollout + release note.

marie (design): thanks — will add final assets and a small acceptance QA list (contrast checks, keyboard nav, screen reader walkthrough). :thumbsup:
